subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should unset Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` become `1024` for all upgraded users, and what explicit opt-out or migration contract is required before merge?
rationale: This is a security hardening default, but it changes existing runtime behavior and the current schema does not accept an unlimited opt-out value, so automation cannot choose the permanent security/compatibility policy.

options.title: Approve default with opt-out
options.body: Require the PR to preserve explicit configured limits, define and document an accepted unlimited opt-out, add focused tests, and show real Docker proof before merge.

options.title: Accept strict cap
options.body: Maintainers may decide upgraded users should always get a PID cap unless they configure a positive replacement value, accepting possible workload breakage as intentional security posture.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep the issue open and close or replace this PR if the permanent default belongs in a broader sandbox resource-limit design.

recommendation.title: Approve default with opt-out
recommendation.body: Require the PR to preserve explicit configured limits, define and document an accepted unlimited opt-out, add focused tests, and show real Docker proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox security hardening history makes this the best available routing candidate for the security/default tradeoff.
